question: to the Commission Pascal Arimont (PPE), Andreas Schwab (PPE), Dan-Ştefan Motreanu (PPE), Olivier Chastel (Renew), Dimitris Tsiodras (PPE), Tomáš Zdechovský (PPE), Christian Doleschal (PPE), Martine Kemp (PPE), Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová (Renew), Rasmus Andresen (Verts/ALE), Benoit Cassart (Renew), Wouter Beke (PPE), Manuela Ripa (PPE), Sabine Verheyen (PPE), François-Xavier Bellamy (PPE), Fernand Kartheiser (NI), Liesbet Sommen (PPE), Elio Di Rupo (S&D), Leila Chaibi (The Left), Thomas Waitz (Verts/ALE), Radan Kanev (PPE), Alexandra Mehnert (PPE), Stéphanie Yon-Courtin (Renew), Branislav Ondruš (NI), Malika Sorel (NI) Subject:

After the German Bundeskartellamt launched an investigation into Amazon’s price control mechanisms in June 2025, the authority issued a ruling on 5 February 2026 stating that the US company must repay EUR 59 million in economic benefits. The authority is concerned that Amazon’s behaviour restricts the competitive process in the marketplace, hinders sellers’ economic viability and entrenches Amazon’s own dominance by blocking other online retailers from offering lower prices. This behaviour is also likely to be a violation of Article 5(3) of the Digital Markets Act1, which prohibits gatekeepers from preventing business users from offering the same products or services via different channels at prices or conditions different from those it offers via the gatekeeper. Commission Executive Vice-President Teresa Ribera has previously said that the Commission is assessing Amazon’s pricing practices and closely coordinating with the Bundeskartellamt on this investigation. 1.
What steps has the Commission taken since July 2025 to ensure that Amazon does not violate Article 5(3) of the Digital Markets Act?
Will the Commission open a formal non-compliance investigation into Amazon?

Considering the seriousness of the risks to market concentration and for the economic viability of independent sellers, will the Commission impose interim measures to ensure that Amazon immediately stops controlling independent sellers’ prices?

answer: (English version) to the Commission Pascal Arimont (PPE), Andreas Schwab (PPE), Dan-Ştefan Motreanu (PPE), Olivier Chastel (Renew), Dimitris Tsiodras (PPE), Tomáš Zdechovský (PPE), Christian Doleschal (PPE), Martine Kemp (PPE), Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová (Renew), Rasmus Andresen (Verts/ALE), Benoit Cassart (Renew), Wouter Beke (PPE), Manuela Ripa (PPE), Sabine Verheyen (PPE), François-Xavier Bellamy (PPE), Fernand Kartheiser (NI), Liesbet Sommen (PPE), Elio Di Rupo (S&D), Leila Chaibi (The Left), Thomas Waitz (Verts/ALE), Radan Kanev (PPE), Alexandra Mehnert (PPE), Stéphanie Yon-Courtin (Renew), Branislav Ondruš (NI), Malika Sorel (NI) (10 March 2026) Subject: German Bundeskartellamt inquiry into Amazon pricing practices After the German Bundeskartellamt launched an investigation into Amazon’s price control mechanisms in June 2025, the authority issued a ruling on 5 February 2026 stating that the US company must repay EUR 59 million in economic benefits. The authority is concerned that Amazon’s behaviour restricts the competitive process in the marketplace, hinders sellers’ economic viability and entrenches Amazon’s own dominance by blocking other online retailers from offering lower prices. This behaviour is also likely to be a violation of Article 5(3) of the Digital Markets Act (1), which prohibits gatekeepers from preventing business users from offering the same products or services via different channels at prices or conditions different from those it offers via the gatekeeper. Commission Executive Vice-President Teresa Ribera has previously said that the Commission is assessing Amazon’s pricing practices and closely coordinating with the Bundeskartellamt on this investigation. 1. What steps has the Commission taken since July 2025 to ensure that Amazon does not violate Article 5(3) of the Digital Markets Act? 2.
Will the Commission open a formal non-compliance investigation into Amazon?

3. Considering the seriousness of the risks to market concentration and for the economic viability of independent sellers, will the Commission impose interim measures to ensure that Amazon immediately stops controlling independent sellers’ prices? (5 May 2026) The Commission is monitoring Amazon’s compliance with Article 5(3) of the Digital Markets Act (DMA) (1), including by investigating Amazon’s pricing practices (2). It has sent several requests for information to Amazon and is in an active regulatory dialogue both with Amazon and interested third parties. At the same time, the Commission has cooperated closely with the Bundeskartellamt within the framework of cooperation and coordination provided under the DMA and competition rules. Article 5(3) DMA does not cover all pricing practices but only those that prevent business users from offering the same products or services via different channels at prices different from those they offer via the gatekeeper. To the extent they amount to an abuse of a dominant position, pricing practices can also run afoul of Article 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU (TFEU) or national equivalent competition laws. For any conduct not covered by the DMA, the Bundeskartellamt can apply the stricter abuse control provisions under Section 19a of the German Competition Act in addition to Article 102 TFEU and national equivalent, which always remain applicable next to the DMA.

Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 September 2022 on contestable and fair markets in the digital sector and amending Directives (EU) 2019/1937 and (EU) 2020/1828 (Digital Markets Act) (OJ L 265, 12.10.2022, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/1925/oj). Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 September 2022 on contestable and fair markets in the digital sector and amending Directives (EU) 2019/1937 and (EU) 2020/1828 (Digital Markets Act), OJ L 265, 12.10.2022, pp. 1-66. This includes the pricing mechanisms the Bundeskartellamt briefly explained under point 4 of the Questions and Answers accompanying the press release for its decision of 5 February 2026, available at https://www.bundeskartellamt.de/SharedDocs/Publikation/EN/Others/Amazon_QandA.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=8 .

The Commission remains committed to ensuring effective implementation and enforcement of the DMA. The Commission continues its supervisory and enforcement work in relation to Amazon’s compliance with the DMA, and it will not hesitate to take any measure necessary if justified by the results of an ongoing investigation.
